title: Artificial intelligence-assisted smartphone thermal imaging for pedicled facial and head-neck flaps: An exploratory feasibility study using ΔT-based proxy perfusion grading

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Artificial intelligence-assisted smartphone thermal imaging for pedicled facial and head-neck flaps: An exploratory feasibility study using ΔT-based proxy perfusion grading》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · para0005】Reliable assessment of flap perfusion remains one of the most critical factors determining surgical success in reconstructive face, head and neck surgery. Pedicled and free skin flaps are essential tools for restoring function and aesthetics following tumor resection, trauma, or chronic wound treatment. However, early detection of perfusion compromise continues to depend largely on subjective clinical parameters such as color, capillary refill, and tissue temperature, which are operator-dependent and may fail to identify early ischemia. 1, 2, 3 The development of an objective, non-invasive, and reproducible method for perfusion assessment is therefore of high clinical relevance.

【Introduction · para0007】Despite these advantages, thermal image interpretation remains qualitative and user-dependent,8 limiting standardization across institutions.9,10 To overcome this limitation, our previous work7 proposed a structured, ΔT-based evaluation algorithm for SBTI in reconstructive surgery of the head and neck. By quantifying temperature differences (ΔT) across predefined flap zones, we previously demonstrated that ΔT values correlate with clinical perfusion assessment. However, ΔT-based grading itself remains an indirect and manually interpreted proxy measure. The present study therefore explores whether thermal image classifications provided by artificial intelligence (AI) demonstrate systematic distributional relationships with manually assigned ΔT-based categories. Our approach establishes SBTI as a reproducible and objective adjunct to clinical monitoring.6,7

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Artificial intelligence-assisted smartphone thermal imaging for pedicled facial and head-neck flaps: An exploratory feasibility study using ΔT-based proxy perfusion grading》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Patient cohort and flap types · para0020】A total of 26 patients undergoing reconstruction with pedicled skin flaps of the face, head and neck were included. The cohort ranged from 42 to 93 years of age. Flap sizes varied substantially (range 1 × 1 cm to 11 × 8 cm) and comprised bilobed flaps (n = 6), Rieger/Hatchet flaps (n = 6), nasolabial/Nelaton flaps (n = 5), frontotemporal or glabella advancement flaps (n = 3), cervicofacial/SCAI flaps (n = 4), and additional rotation-advancement designs (n = 2). All flaps demonstrated intraoperative clinical perfusion. Postoperative complications occurred in 1 out of 26 cases (3.8%), requiring revision surgery.

【Thermal characteristics across flap designs · para0022】Nasal reconstructions, especially at the alar region, frequently appeared thermographically cooler due to the intrinsic temperature gradient of acral facial sites. This was particularly evident in patient 72T4503 × 2 (Nelaton flap), where a relatively low AI perfusion probability score (∼32–38%) occurred despite excellent clinical perfusion. These findings illustrate that anatomical location is a dominant confounder and limits direct comparability of absolute ΔT or AI-derived perfusion probability score across regions.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Artificial intelligence-assisted smartphone thermal imaging for pedicled facial and head-neck flaps: An exploratory feasibility study using ΔT-based proxy perfusion grading》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusion · para0039】This exploratory pilot study demonstrates the technical feasibility of AI-assisted interpretation of smartphone-based thermal images in pedicled facial and head-and-neck flaps. However, no meaningful quantitative agreement with manually derived ΔT-based reference grading was observed. Given the absence of validated perfusion ground truth, the small and imbalanced dataset, and substantial anatomical heterogeneity, the present findings should be interpreted as preliminary workflow feasibility only. Future studies require radiometric thermal imaging, objective multimodal perfusion references, anatomically stratified cohorts, and substantially larger datasets before clinically meaningful AI-derived perfusion assessment can be established.

【Results · abstract-3-1】Thermal patterns varied substantially by flap type, thickness, and anatomical region. Random-pattern glabellar, nasal, and alar flaps showed physiologically lower surface temperatures and correspondingly reduced ΔT- and AI-derived prediction probabilities despite uneventful healing. No statistically significant correlation was observed between AI-derived perfusion probabilities and manually derived ΔT grades.
